questions.prompt: Why do Zig standard library data structures and I/O functions accept a `std.mem.Allocator` parameter?

options.text: Because Zig has no OS heap
To make every allocation explicit, swappable (arena, fixed-buffer, leak-detecting), and testable for OOM

questions.prompt: What does `std.heap.DebugAllocator(.{})` (or `GeneralPurposeAllocator`) detect automatically in `deinit()`?

options.text: Memory leaks and double-frees during development and `zig test`

questions.prompt: When is `std.heap.ArenaAllocator` the best choice?

options.text: For long-lived caches that grow forever
When many small allocations share one phase/request lifetime and can all be freed together in O(1) via `arena.deinit()`
When writing kernel interrupt handlers with no heap

questions.prompt: Select all standard Zig allocators and their primary use cases. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: `std.testing.allocator` for automatic leak detection in unit tests
`std.heap.FixedBufferAllocator` for stack/preallocated buffers with zero OS syscalls

questions.prompt: Match each Zig build optimization mode to its trade-off.

columns.label: Fast compilation, full debug info, all safety checks enabled
Optimized machine code while keeping bounds, overflow, and null safety checks
Maximum speed with runtime safety checks stripped

questions.prompt: What does `@typeInfo(T)` enable in Zig `comptime` metaprogramming?

options.text: Inspecting struct fields, enum tags, pointers, and function signatures at compile time to generate serializers/ORMs/CLIs

questions.prompt: What does `build.zig` use to describe targets, dependencies, and build steps?

options.text: Standard Zig code (`pub fn build(b: *std.Build) void`) compiled and executed by `zig build`

questions.prompt: What does `zig build --summary all` (or `b.addTest(...)`) integrate into `build.zig`?

options.text: Compiling executables, running unit tests, and reporting step summaries

questions.prompt: How does Zig's `@cImport({ @cInclude("sqlite3.h"); })` work?

options.text: Requires writing manual FFI wrappers for every C struct
Translates C headers directly into Zig declarations at compile time using Zig's built-in Clang frontend

questions.prompt: Why can `zig cc` and `zig build` cross-compile C/C++/Zig to Linux, macOS, and Windows from one machine without separate toolchains?

options.text: Zig bundles Clang/LLD plus libc headers/stubs (glibc, musl, mingw-w64) for major targets

questions.prompt: Why should C-ABI structs in Zig use `extern struct` instead of normal `struct`?

options.text: Normal Zig `struct` allows the compiler to reorder fields for packing; `extern struct` guarantees exact C ABI field layout

questions.prompt: What is the key difference between `extern struct` and `packed struct` in Zig?

options.text: `extern struct` follows C ABI byte padding/alignment; `packed struct` packs fields tightly at the bit level with a backing integer

questions.prompt: What does `@bitCast(value)` require?

options.text: Source and destination types must have the exact same bit size (`@bitSizeOf`) at compile time

questions.prompt: Select all techniques that prevent memory leaks and double-frees in production Zig. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Pair every allocation with `defer alloc.free(...)` or `errdefer alloc.free(...)`
Test all error/OOM paths with `std.testing.allocator` and `std.testing.checkAllAllocationFailures`

questions.prompt: What does `std.testing.checkAllAllocationFailures` test?

options.text: That your function cleans up all partial allocations cleanly without leaking when any allocation returns `error.OutOfMemory`

questions.prompt: What is a common pitfall when returning a slice pointing to a local stack array (`var buf: [64]u8 = ...; return buf[0..n];`)?

options.text: Dangling pointer / undefined behavior after the function returns and the stack frame is popped

questions.prompt: In Zig, how do `std.Io.Writer` / `anytype` writers enable zero-allocation streaming?

options.text: Functions take a writer interface/generic and stream bytes directly to files, sockets, or fixed buffers

questions.prompt: What does `std.atomic.Value(usize)` provide for multi-threaded Zig programs?

options.text: Lock-free atomic loads, stores, and read-modify-write operations with explicit memory ordering (`.seq_cst`, `.acquire`, `.release`)

questions.prompt: What does `std.Thread.Mutex` paired with `mutex.lock(); defer mutex.unlock();` guarantee?

options.text: That the mutex is always released on any normal or error `return` path

questions.prompt: Match each Zig FFI/systems construct to its use case.

columns.label: Imports C headers directly into Zig
Matches C ABI field layout and padding
Exposes a Zig function with C linkage in a library

questions.prompt: What does `zig fmt --check .` do in a CI pipeline?

options.text: Exits non-zero if any `.zig` file is not formatted canonically, without modifying files

questions.prompt: What does `comptime` duck-typing (`writer: anytype`) trade off compared to explicit interfaces?

options.text: Zero vtable overhead and full inlining, at the cost of monomorphizing per concrete type and checking methods at instantiation

questions.prompt: How does `std.mem.Allocator` achieve runtime polymorphism without language-level `interface` or `class` keywords?

options.text: A `ptr: *anyopaque` plus a `*const VTable` struct of function pointers

questions.prompt: What does `@compileLog(x)` do when debugging `comptime` code?

options.text: Emits a compile-time log of `x` and intentionally stops compilation so you don't accidentally ship debug logs

questions.prompt: Select all valid ways Zig prevents common C footguns. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Optionals `?T` separate nullable values from non-null pointers `*T`
No implicit integer-to-pointer or float-to-int conversions
Slices carry `.len` and are bounds-checked in `Debug`/`ReleaseSafe`
Switch statements must be exhaustive with no implicit fallthrough

questions.prompt: What does `align(64)` on a variable or struct field enforce?

options.text: 64-byte memory alignment (e.g., to avoid false sharing across CPU cache lines or meet SIMD requirements)

questions.prompt: What does `std.heap.page_allocator` do on every `alloc` call?

options.text: Makes an OS virtual-memory syscall (`mmap`/`VirtualAlloc`) allocating whole memory pages (e.g. 4 KiB+)

questions.prompt: What does `const val = @import("builtin");` provide?

options.text: Compile-time target OS, CPU architecture, endianness, and build mode (`builtin.mode`, `builtin.os.tag`)

questions.prompt: What does `std.os.linux` / `std.posix` vs `std.fs` / `std.net` represent?

options.text: `std.fs`/`std.net` provide portable cross-platform APIs; `std.posix`/`std.os.linux` expose low-level OS syscalls

questions.prompt: What does `b.addOptions()` in `build.zig` allow?

options.text: Passing build-time configuration values into Zig source via `@import("config")`

questions.prompt: Select all true statements about `build.zig.zon`. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Declares package name, version, and dependencies with content hashes
Used by `zig fetch` and `zig build` for reproducible dependency fetching

questions.prompt: Why does `std.BufMap` or `ArenaAllocator` simplify building a string-heavy CLI or compiler pass?

options.text: They own duplicated strings and free them all in one `deinit()`, avoiding complex per-string ownership tracking

questions.prompt: What does `@ptrFromInt(0x1000)` vs `@intFromPtr(ptr)` do?

options.text: Converts between raw integer addresses and pointers explicitly (for MMIO, OS kernels, or tagged pointers)

questions.prompt: What does `volatile` on a pointer (`*volatile u32`) tell the Zig optimizer?

options.text: Make it thread-safe across CPU cores
Do not elide, cache, or reorder reads/writes to this memory (essential for memory-mapped hardware registers)

questions.prompt: Match each Zig safety or systems feature to its purpose.

columns.label: Tests every OOM path for leaks
Frees all phase allocations together in O(1)
Prevents optimizer from eliding MMIO reads/writes

questions.prompt: What does `std.io.BufferedWriter` / `std.io.bufferedWriter` improve when writing many small chunks to a file or socket?

options.text: Batches small writes in memory to drastically reduce expensive OS `write` syscalls

questions.prompt: Why should you call `try bw.flush();` before closing a buffered writer?

options.text: Unflushed bytes in the buffer would otherwise be lost when the underlying file is closed

questions.prompt: What does `@memcpy(dst, src)` require in Zig?

options.text: `dst` and `src` must have the same length and must not overlap (use `std.mem.copyForwards`/`copyBackwards` if overlapping)

questions.prompt: What does `std.mem.zeroSecure(secret_buf)` (or `std.crypto.utils.secureZero`) do that a plain loop might fail to do?

options.text: Guarantees the compiler will NOT optimize away the zeroing of sensitive key/password buffers before freeing

questions.prompt: In `ReleaseFast` mode, what happens if an array index is out of bounds?

options.text: Undefined behavior because runtime safety checks are disabled—use `ReleaseSafe` unless benchmarks prove `ReleaseFast` is required

questions.prompt: Select all production-ready Zig engineering practices. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Prefer `ReleaseSafe` for network-facing services unless `ReleaseFast` is justified
Use `errdefer` for every multi-step resource initialization
Use `page_allocator` directly for every individual node in a linked list
Run `zig build test` with `std.testing.allocator` and `zig fmt --check` in CI

questions.prompt: What does `zig translate-c foo.h` do?

options.text: Outputs readable Zig source code equivalent to the C header for inspection or permanent conversion
